subject: English
passage:
[Figure 1]

Environmental scientist Amelia Everett and her colleague Cristobal Vasquez surveyed small-scale renewable energy installations in three coastal districts of Portugal—which features rocky cliffs in the north, a densely populated central estuary, and sandy lowlands in the south—to learn more about ownership patterns, including the types of energy systems most commonly installed. In some districts, community-owned installations were found to be especially prominent for specific types of energy systems and even constituted the majority of installations of those types; for instance, ______
prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the example?

choices.A: most of the installations of wind turbines and most of the installations of solar panels in southern Portugal were community-owned.
choices.B: more community-owned installations in central Portugal were of micro-hydro systems than of wind turbines.
choices.C: most of the installations of solar panels in northern and southern Portugal were community-owned.
choices.D: a relatively equal proportion of community-owned installations across the three districts of Portugal were of wind turbines.

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer because it uses data from the graph to effectively complete the example of Everett and Vasquez's findings concerning community-owned installations in some districts of coastal Portugal. The graph presents values for the percentage of small-scale renewable installations that are community-owned, by energy system type and district. The graph shows that of the installations of solar panels, 58% in northern Portugal and 54% in southern Portugal are community-owned; in other words, most of those installations are community-owned, which exemplifies the idea that community-owned installations make up the majority (more than half) of installations of specific energy system types in some districts.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect because it doesn't effectively complete the example; it simply states that a relatively equal proportion of community-owned installations across the three districts are wind turbines, which doesn't address the value for that proportion and thus doesn't show that a majority (more than half) of installations of certain energy system types are community-owned.
